title: Each Row Shows Its Department's Top Earner
description:
For every employee, report their own name alongside the name of the **highest-paid person in their own department** — repeated on every row of that department.

Name the columns `name` and `dept_top_earner`. Return the result in any order.
hint: FIRST_VALUE always returns the first row of the frame — order the partition by salary descending so "first" means "highest paid", and use a full-partition frame so every row (not just later ones) sees the same answer.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
One employee per department — each is their own top earner
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Eve','E',90000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Department with no employees
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Ghost','Nowhere');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: All employees earn the same salary — everyone is top earner
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','E',100000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'C','E',100000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Single department with multiple employees — clear top earner
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Low','E',50000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Mid','E',75000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Top','E',150000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Tie for top earner in a department — FIRST_VALUE picks first by id
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',150000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',150000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Cara','E',120000,1,1,'2020-01-01');
